er-crit-coop.notes: Sibling Elden Ring DLL mod on the same fromsoftware-rs SDK. Shares the platform (toolchain, release shape, DLL entry/task-hook pattern); never the mod behavior, package identity (Cargo name/version/description), or README prose. er-crit-coop is frozen, so most flow is from here -> there, and only for fixes worth having.

dotfiles.notes: Shares only the sync skill itself.

stillair.notes: Custom ceiling fan project (docs + Rust ESP32 firmware). Took the next/wrap session-continuity skills from here, stripped of fleet/rig; it runs solo.

resources.notes: Shared platform ignores (target/, reference/, deploy artifacts); each repo adds its own entries.

Shared: release-profile ideas and the fromsoftware-rs pin discipline (both SDK crates at one git commit; verify layouts before bumping either repo's pin). Owned: name/version/description and each mod's own deps. This repo is a workspace: profile in the root manifest, deps in crates/unseamless-coop/Cargo.toml; er-crit-coop is a single crate. Release profiles intentionally differ on panic: unwind here (the catch_unwind firewall), abort there.
Same shape: tag push -> mingw cross-compile -> GitHub release. Artifacts differ (DLL + launcher + dist bundle here; single DLL there). Port CI improvements, keep artifact lists per repo.
Same job (install the built DLL into the game), different install model: dinput8 proxy + launcher here (wrapped by rig.sh), Elden Mod Loader mods/ there. Port safety improvements only.
Common origin, intentionally diverged: this logger is diagnostics-integrated (RunInfo header, rotated logs); er-crit-coop's stays minimal. Port bugfixes, not features.
Shared: the DllMain pattern and its hard safety invariants (ATTACH-only, init thread off the loader lock, wait_for_instance -> run_recurring -> mem::forget). Owned: everything the mod actually does.
Shared toolchain/build story (cross-compile from Linux, mingw, .text-size equivalence check); workflow and repo specifics are owned.

Shared shape only (gather ground truth -> enumerate candidates -> recommend -> record in docs/STATE.md). This repo's version adds fleet/worker spawning and rig batching; stillair's is solo and points at its own gating docs. Port procedure improvements, never the fleet/rig steps.

Shared shape only (sweep learnings -> decide next -> rewrite STATE.md wholesale -> commit -> sign off). This repo's version has fleet/rig rules; stillair's is solo with its own learning-routing table.
Same tag-driven release procedure; this repo adds its own rules (pre-1.0 versioning, canonical notes format) that don't apply there. Port procedural improvements both ways.
